Yemen Financial Inclusion Evidence

Preserve the meaning of the evidence before comparing the numbers.

Every published figure has been checked against the source it is attributed to. A figure that could not be verified is withheld, and a figure known only from a secondary source is labelled as secondary. Each figure keeps its unit, population, period and geography; derived figures can be recomputed from recorded inputs; and material corrections are recorded. The method exists to prevent one common failure: treating different people, accounts, providers, periods, geographies and programme records as if they measured the same thing.

Start with a questionVerify evidence
Understand → Explore → Verify

This resource presents the strongest defensible answer while keeping scope, limits and source visible.

01
Evidence

Start with what is being measured

People, accounts, active accounts, savers, borrowers, providers, service points, terminals, transactions, balances, programme beneficiaries and reform milestones are different analytical objects. The method never assumes that one can stand in for another.

02
What it means

Evidence from several dates can be valid at once

Population surveys, administrative records, provider rosters, regulations, project milestones and programme results update at different times. This resource preserves observation or fieldwork dates separately from release dates so a newer publication is not mistaken for a newer measurement.

03
What it means

What the evidence covers — and what it does not

Coverage differs by topic. A few topics have current observations: the formal status of providers under CBY-Aden lists, bank credit and other monetary statistics, and remittance prices in two corridors. Most people-side topics rest on the latest representative survey wave (fieldwork 2022–23) or on 2014 values, and several — frequency of use, financial resilience, digital capability, affordability and differences by age — are defined in the 2021 survey data but not yet estimated. Payments, regulation and consumer protection are evidenced mainly through administrative and regulatory records, which show systems and rules rather than use or outcomes. This resource has no current Yemen evidence on service reliability, the geography of operating access points, inclusion by displacement or disability status, digital fraud, insurance or pensions. Gaps are shown as gaps: they are not filled with other countries' figures, and each is linked to a measurement priority.

04
Analysis

How evidence is accepted, and in what role

A source enters the evidence base when its original link and date can be recorded and its content can be checked against the source itself; its publisher, issuer and reuse terms are recorded when they have been confirmed. A source's role is recorded for each use rather than once for the source: the same report can be primary factual evidence for one record and context for another. The roles are primary factual evidence, a dated status event, Yemen analytical literature, a global method reference and context. The kind of document — a law, decision, survey, dataset or report — is recorded separately, and no numerical quality score is assigned. Primary evidence and status events support public figures directly. A figure known only from a secondary source appears only when it is attributed and labelled as secondary. Analytical literature is attributed to its authors, and global references inform method without standing in for Yemen evidence. A figure that cannot be verified against its stated source is withheld.

05
System context

Measuring in a divided, conflict-affected setting

Four features of Yemen change how evidence is read. Central-bank authority has been divided since 2016, so official lists, decisions and statistics carry the scope of the authority that issued them. Rial values can differ between monetary areas, so a nominal figure is read with its valuation basis where the source records it. Survey coverage is incomplete: the latest Findex wave excluded areas holding about 23% of the population and replaced more than a quarter of its sampling units. And programme data describe programme populations. None of this explains a result by itself: conflict is context for interpretation, not a cause the evidence has established.

06
Analysis

Uncertainty is stated, not manufactured

Survey estimates carry sampling and coverage uncertainty. Where a source publishes a confidence interval or standard error, it is reported with the estimate. Where it does not, no interval, standard error or significance test is added unless it can be reproduced from the survey's own weights and design. A derived value, such as the difference between two percentages, keeps the precision of its inputs, with no added decimal places, and small differences between estimates are not read as a ranking.

07
Analysis

Derived evidence must be reproducible

When this resource calculates a gap, share, ratio, revision or other derived measure, it records the inputs and method needed to reproduce the calculation. A derivation cannot create coverage, comparability or causal meaning that the inputs did not contain.

08
System context

Comparison is conditional on compatibility

Before values share a scale, this resource checks definition, period, geography, population or base, unit, source coverage and method. A material mismatch stays visible and can block a common scale. The purpose is not to prevent comparison; it is to prevent a false one.

09
Evidence

How an item’s evidence state affects what you see

An item’s evidence state — for example observed, derived, historical, conflicting, superseded or corrected — determines how it is described and whether it appears in search and Compare. An item whose state is unclear is not presented as reusable evidence until the state is resolved.

10
What this does not establish

What the method does not claim

Traceability is not certainty. A primary source can still be old; a recent administrative record may not measure people; a representative survey may not support governorate estimates; a correct calculation may still use a narrow base. The method preserves those limits rather than turning them into one confidence score.

11
Verify the evidence

Correction is part of the evidence trail

When a source is revised or an error is found, the public evidence record is corrected without losing its stable identity. New or conflicting evidence is checked against the original source before it changes a public record. If it materially changes the interpretation, the current record states what changed and why; if the conflict cannot be resolved, the uncertainty remains visible. Superseded evidence remains traceable when public retention is appropriate.

12
Verify the evidence

Challenge the answer

From a public answer, open the evidence record and inspect the original source (its link or version), unit, population or calculation base, geography, period, method and reuse rights and publication status. Compare it with other evidence only when definitions permit. An unresolved source conflict stays visible rather than being averaged, harmonized or silently repaired. If something is wrong or incomplete, use the correction channel and cite the stable evidence ID.

13
Measurement framework

Composite scores follow survey-round-specific rules

Composite financial-literacy measures combine several constructs and follow scoring rules specific to the survey round that produced them. Reproducing a score therefore requires the definitions, question set and calculation rules for that round; carrying scoring rules across editions can change what the measure represents. A financial-literacy score is not an access rate.

Related evidence records

Accounts and transactions are not unique people

Administrative accounts, e-wallet subscribers and payment transactions are not equivalent to unique people measured by Findex.

Does not establish: Dividing administrative counts by population does not produce a share of people unless a documented unique-person method exists; no such share is established here.
Open evidence record →

Evidence freshness differs by domain

The evidence here is not equally current across domains: several payments/regulatory observations are from 2025–2026, while key representative people-side evidence is older.

Does not establish: Older evidence is not invalid because of its age, and recent administrative evidence does not measure current financial inclusion across the population.
Open evidence record →

Latest monthly POS release listed by CBY-Aden: January 2026 (page checked 26 September 2026)

The payments page of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) lists monthly POS releases from March 2025 to January 2026. When the page was checked on 26 September 2026, January 2026 was the latest release listed; no later month is inferred.

Does not establish: It does not show that POS activity stopped after January 2026; it identifies only the latest monthly release listed on the payments page of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) when checked on 26 September 2026.
Open evidence record →

Informative history without a continuous annual series

The historical microfinance evidence is informative but does not form a continuous annual series. This resource keeps the exact quarterly and year-end points, anomalies, years known only through a reference in another source, and years with no data, rather than filling the gaps.

Does not establish: A year with no observation does not indicate zero microfinance activity, and the observations do not establish a trend across the missing years.
Open evidence record →

What the Yemen Findex 2021 study contains

The Yemen Global Findex 2021 study file has 1,000 respondents and 113 variables; Yemen fieldwork ran from 7 November 2022 to 9 January 2023 and all population estimates require survey weights.

Does not establish: Raw case percentages in the study documentation are not population estimates.
Open evidence record →

Raw case shares are not population estimates

World Bank variable pages expose raw sample case counts and percentages for the Yemen Findex file, but explicitly warn that those figures cannot be interpreted as summary statistics of the population of interest.

Does not establish: The raw, unweighted case percentages shown on the World Bank variable pages are not estimates for Yemen's adult population and are not reported in this resource.
Open evidence record →

Geographic coverage limits of the latest Findex wave

The latest Yemen Findex wave excludes Al Baydaa, Al Jawf, Mareb, Sadah, Socotra and several districts elsewhere; the source states excluded areas represent approximately 23% of the population, and over one-fourth of primary sampling units were replaced during fieldwork.

Does not establish: The wave does not cover all of Yemen, and its results cannot be used to map financial inclusion by governorate.
Open evidence record →

Demand-side measures defined; custom estimates not yet published

A 32-metric demand-side panel has been specified across access, barriers, digital use, saving, borrowing, resilience, remittances, income flows, financial worry and connectivity. Custom weighted estimates are not published yet because they require authorized respondent-level data, correct survey weights and successful reproduction of the official benchmark values.

Does not establish: The 32 specified measures are planned, not measured: none is yet a published indicator, because the weighted estimates have not been reproduced and checked against official benchmarks.
Open evidence record →

A smoother published path is a methods question, not a conclusion

In the CBY-Aden Annual Report 2025, the published remittance series rises with unusually similar annual growth rates across overlapping years. That pattern is useful for method scrutiny, but it does not establish smoothing, interpolation or low real-world volatility.

Does not establish: The pattern does not establish smoothing, interpolation or low real-world volatility.
Open evidence record →

A reconstruction programme is documented; the exact CBY formula is not

IMF documents a 2024–2025 external-sector statistical reconstruction effort with CBY-Aden, including a demographic-behavioural personal-transfer model where informal-channel data were limited. This establishes method context, not the exact formula or scope used for every remittance value in the CBY-Aden Annual Report 2025.

Does not establish: The public evidence does not establish the exact formula behind the values in the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) Annual Report 2025, or that CBY-Aden and IMF levels share the same scope.
Open evidence record →

The 2023 valuation change has a precedent and cannot be called the “first ever”

Market-rate valuation of foreign-currency accounts has documented precedent in Yemen from 1996, while CBY-Aden separately documents a January-2023 valuation/reporting change affecting current banking series. The two episodes should not be assumed to use identical standards.

Does not establish: The January 2023 change was not the first market-rate valuation in Yemen, since a precedent is documented from 1996, and the evidence does not show that the historical and contemporary standards are identical.
Open evidence record →

A public interface is not the same thing as the underlying dataset

World Bank public remittance interfaces do not expose Yemen history uniformly. One interface, reviewed on 10 September 2026, showed an older span of years, while other World Bank interfaces and earlier documented retrievals contained later observations. The difference reflects what each interface displays and how its data can be traced; it is not evidence that later underlying data are absent.

Does not establish: The difference does not show that data were deleted or withdrawn, or why any correction was made, and one public interface's observations are not a substitute for another's.
Open evidence record →

A stable remittance ratio exists; its meaning remains unknown

Over 2021–2024, the ratio of the remittance series in the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) Annual Report 2025 to the IMF 2025 Article IV series is 1.838 in every year, and the two growth paths are almost identical when indexed to 2021 = 100. The public evidence does not establish what that ratio represents, so it is a numerical regularity with no documented explanation, not a conversion rule.

Does not establish: The 1.838 ratio is not a population, geography, informal-share or coverage conversion.
Open evidence record →

A change in an external position is not automatically a transaction

Changes in Yemen's external asset or liability positions should be decomposed into transactions, exchange-rate changes, other price changes and other volume changes before they are interpreted as financial flows. The change in international investment position (IIP) stocks between opening and closing dates is not, on its own, a measure of balance-of-payments transactions.

Does not establish: The difference between opening and closing international investment position stocks is not, on its own, a measure of balance-of-payments transactions.
Open evidence record →

BPM7 updates the standard; it does not rewrite Yemen’s statistical history overnight

BPM7 is the updated global external-sector statistical standard, but implementation is a multi-year transition. Yemen's historical series should keep the standard and version under which their sources published them until an explicit conversion or revision is published.

Does not establish: The release of BPM7 does not mean that Yemen's historical data have been restated under it, or that Yemeni sources have already adopted it.
Open evidence record →

How many respondents answered each Findex question

Weighted estimates for the 2021 wave have not yet been produced, so no values are shown. When they are published, each will be accompanied by the number of respondents who gave a valid answer, the number of missing or invalid answers, and a note where a question was asked only of a sub-group; these counts describe the sample and are not population estimates.

Raw case percentages are not population prevalence rates, and indicators are not ranked by them.
Open evidence record →

Which historical Findex measures can be compared with the latest wave

A comparability map linking 36 historical Findex measures to the measures specified for the latest wave, while separating publishable historical values from latest-wave measures whose required computation is not yet complete.

A crosswalk identifies conceptual comparability; it does not make every historical and latest-wave metric numerically interchangeable, and latest-wave values remain unavailable until the required computation and quality checks are complete.
Open evidence record →
